items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: that Coleman Hawkins’ record of “Body and Soul” probably was one of the biggest records ever sold.

ctx.x: I’ll tell you the nearest way I can describe it is I don’t know who I’m talking to and I don’t know what I’m going to say. That’s how it is with playing. I haven’t got the slightest idea what you’re going to play but that’s coming out like I’m talking right now. I’m talking to you on a subject, I’m playing on chord changes and the song. I hear the song in my head. For example, I always tell everybody that, or young kids that want to play for me and show me how good they are or want to study: Don’t play the…

secrets I found out about writing in the bebop era. They used to take all the great songs and, like “How High the Moon” and “Groovin’ High” and take the chord changes and write their own songs in them. Why should we be giving them all the money, you know? You know what’s wild, if you want to think back going way back, that Coleman Hawkins’ record of “Body and Soul” probably was one of the biggest records ever sold.
